name: Albania
summary_text: Albania is workable for trans visitors. Nothing is criminalised; a National LGBTI Action Plan (2021–2027) is in force (implementation is admittedly flawed); and the UN Independent Expert on SOGI conducted a full country visit in July 2024 — a sign of government openness unusual for the region. Tirana hosts an annual Pride. For a visitor: no legal exposure, no bathroom laws, no documented police targeting; the realistic risk is social hostility outside Tirana and along more conservative rural areas. EU candidate status is driving slow alignment.

sources.claim_summary: End-of-mission statement of the UN Independent Expert on SOGI after his 1-12 July 2024 visit to Albania (Tirana plus five municipalities). Assesses implementation of national and international standards on violence and discrimination based on sexual orientation and gender identity; notes cooperation from the government and identifies challenges and good practices.

ILGA-Europe Annual Review 2024 (covering 2023) chapter on Albania. Documents hate violence against trans people and sex workers (ten cases reported), LGBTI people's limited access to state services due to discrimination (civil society filling gaps with food packages, bill payments, reimbursement of documentation costs for IDs and passports), education barriers (30% of LGBTI respondents unable to complete compulsory education), and successful discrimination complaints.

Full report (A/HRC/59/43/Add.1, June 2025) of the UN Independent Expert on SOGI following the Albania visit. Evaluates Albania's adherence to human rights standards for LGBT people, examines the situation of lesbian, gay, bisexual and gender-diverse persons in depth, and makes recommendations on violence and discrimination.

sources.title: No gay marriage for Albania | PinkNews
sources.claim_summary: PinkNews (Feb 2010): Albania passed an anti-discrimination law covering sexual orientation (but not same-sex marriage); homosexuality carried a 10-year sentence until 1995; welcomed by Albanian gay-rights groups and ILGA-Europe as a regional example.

sources.title: Fushata e LGBT në gjimnaze, Luçiano Boci: Grupime me axhendë të dyshimtë, revoltuese
sources.claim_summary: Koha Jonë (Albanian, 2021): Democratic Party MP Luçiano Boçi called LGBT awareness meetings in Tirana high schools 'groups with a dubious agenda' and 'revolting' - example of anti-LGBT political rhetoric in Albania.

sources.title: Nard Ndoka: Skandal i tmerrshëm që LGBT diskutojnë në shkolla “vlerat” e tyre
sources.claim_summary: Koha Jonë (Albanian, 2021): politician Nard Ndoka called LGBT school meetings a 'terrible scandal' and claimed an 'LGBT government' was favouring the community in housing, education and employment - example of hostile political discourse.

sources.title: Albanian MP Reprimanded for Gay Slur | Balkan Insight
sources.claim_summary: Balkan Insight (Oct 2011): Albania's Anti-Discrimination Commissioner reprimanded ruling-party MP Tritan Shehu for saying in parliament that 'homosexuality is disease and should be treated with hormones' - the commissioner urged parliament to guarantee LGBT community participation; homosexuality decriminalised in 1995.
